requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

acceptanceCriteria.text: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member of a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly builds cleanly and gets a generated resolver.
The other trigger-matrix shapes (non-generic struct, generic or non-generic class, non-generic record struct) keep working as before.
No CS8785 or AD0001 warning is produced for these shapes.

decisionBrief.text: The change is meant to stop the generator and analyzer crash for a closed generic value type coming from a referenced assembly, while leaving the other trigger-matrix shapes as they were.
The AI's new regression tests fail on the base source and pass on the patch. The full recorded generator suite passes on the patch.
The existing generator suite also passed on the base commit, so the patch did not start from a broken baseline.
The AI says the patch only reports a diagnostic when its location belongs to the compilation being analyzed, so diagnostics for members declared in referenced assemblies are dropped.
A local hand-applied crash-only comparison still reports MsgPack004 diagnostics for an unkeyed member of a referenced structure; the AI patch reports none for that test.
The suppression policy is not requested by the requirement, and whether it changes diagnostics in other consumer scenarios was not checked.
The crash-only comparison is our hand-applied approximation of the reference fix, not a run of that reference patch.
The two-project build reproduction was not run, so the requirement is not confirmed end to end outside the test harness.
The README and MsgPack004 documentation say diagnostics for referenced types are reported by the defining assembly. That holds only if that dependency runs the analyzer, which was not checked.

One AI claim is contradicted because a cited comparison probe expected the opposite outcome, and one is unsupported because a single named test does not match the recorded runs. Neither classification by itself shows that the claim's prose is false.

The model originally listed the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull change as outside the crash fix. The recorded diff shows it is one of the two live unsafe declaration-reference sites the patch replaces, so that item was withdrawn; the raw proposal is preserved.

claims.text: The constructor now wraps the caller-supplied diagnostic reporter so that every diagnostic is passed through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation before being reported.
claims.modelNote: Wrapping happens only when reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is non-null.
claims.statusReason: The citation resolves. The claim describes code; no executed check is needed or implied.

claims.text: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops a diagnostic unless its location is in source and its syntax tree belongs to the compilation being analyzed, so diagnostics for metadata-only members are not reported.
claims.modelNote: This is the mechanism that avoids reporting against a location that does not exist.
claims.statusReason: The citation resolves. The claim describes code; no executed check is needed or implied.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic site now uses DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() instead of indexing [0], so a member with no source declaration yields a null location rather than throwing.
claims.modelNote: The null location is then filtered out by ReportIfLocatedInCompilation.
claims.statusReason: The citation resolves. The claim describes code; no executed check is needed or implied.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic site now obtains its location from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation, which returns null when the property has no PropertyDeclarationSyntax in source, instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].
claims.statusReason: The citation resolves. The claim describes code; no executed check is needed or implied.

claims.modelNote: Fails in CHK3 (base source) and passes in CHK2.

claims.text: GenericsFormatterTests.ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember covers a referenced generic struct with an unkeyed public member and asserts no warning diagnostics and resolver generation, i.e. the member diagnostic is not reported against the consuming compilation.

refusals.question: Should the analyzer silently suppress diagnostics for members declared in referenced assemblies, or should it surface them in some other way (e.g. a single informational diagnostic on the consuming type)?
refusals.whyAiRefused: This is a product/UX decision about analyzer behavior that the requirement does not specify; the change picks suppression.

positions.label: Accept suppression of diagnostics from referenced code for this change.
Require a visible diagnostic or a narrower crash-only fix.
Needs a source-generator owner to judge the diagnostic policy.

refusals.question: Is the README and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md wording about diagnostics being reported by the defining assembly accurate for all consumers (e.g. when the referenced assembly was built without the analyzer)?
refusals.whyAiRefused: Documentation accuracy for scenarios outside the test harness is a judgment call for the owner.

positions.label: Accept the documentation assumption as an explicit limitation for this change.
Require the documentation to qualify the analyzer assumption.
Needs a documentation owner to judge accuracy for consumers.
